penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Provisioning sandboxed GitHub agent accounts and gating PRs requires per-customer configuration, OAuth setup, and security review — not automatable by Claude prompts alone.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Security/DevOps tooling sales to engineering teams typically requires a demo or onboarding call to establish trust before purchase.

rationale: The buyer is real — DevOps leads and platform engineers at AI-adopting companies have genuine need for sandboxed agent accounts — and they do pay for security tooling. However, the product is fundamentally infrastructure: provisioning GitHub org structures, managing OAuth apps, and enforcing PR gates requires deep GitHub API integration, per-customer setup, and ongoing security judgment that cannot be delivered by Claude prompts and a landing page. Operational autonomy is very low, and buildability with this factory's tooling is near-zero. With penalties the total drops to 2.4.
solution_plan: This is not viable for a solo non-technical operator using this factory. Building a managed GitHub agent-account provisioning service would require custom OAuth integrations, GitHub App registration per customer, and security-sensitive configuration that the factory cannot safely automate. Even if a landing page and intake form could capture leads, actual delivery would require Youval to manually provision each customer's GitHub org structure — turning this into a consulting service, not a product. Recommend dropping unless a no-code GitHub automation platform (e.g. a GitHub App marketplace product) emerges that removes the per-customer build burden.
notes: Failing build gates: operational_autonomy (3 < 7 required), buildability_with_ai (3 < 6 required). The core delivery loop is infrastructure work that cannot be delegated to Claude.
